entities.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the speaker, who says he created humankind. The LORD source tag identifies the same divine bearer.

name_review_base.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the speaker, who refers to humankind as “whom I created.” The LORD source tag supports identification with the God named Yahweh in the Genesis 2:22 proposal.

review.translation: [Then|0] [Yahweh|1] [said|0], “[I will wipe away|2] [humankind|4,3] [whom|5] [I created|6] [from|7] [the surface of|8] [the ground|9], [from humans|10] [to|11] [land animals|12], [to|13] [crawling creatures|14], [and to|15] [the birds of|16] [the sky|17], [for|18] [I regret|19] [that|20] [I made them|21].”

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר. The first-person verb אֶמְחֶה (“I will blot out”) begins his direct speech.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה means “Yahweh said.” In the ensuing speech, בָּרָאתִי (“I created”) identifies the named speaker as the creator of humankind.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun without prefix or suffix, serving as the subject of the third-person masculine singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: YHWH names humanity as the direct object (אֶת הָאָדָם) and extends the decree to livestock, creeping things, and birds. מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה identifies the surface from which they will be wiped.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular. The verbal prefix אֶ־ marks the speaker as the subject. There is no pronominal suffix.
analysis.sense: Wipe out living beings from the face of the earth.

analysis.evidence: In אֶמְחֶה אֶת הָאָדָם, “I will blot out humankind,” אֶת marks the definite noun הָאָדָם as the direct object of אֶמְחֶה.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאָדָם as the object of אֶמְחֶה, “I will wipe out.” The phrase מֵאָדָם עַד בְּהֵמָה, “from humans to beasts,” identifies humans as a class and confirms the collective reading.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הָ־. Used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר בָּרָאתִי, “humankind whom I created,” אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause in which הָאָדָם supplies the understood object of בָּרָאתִי, “I created.”
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר בָּרָאתִי, “humankind whom I created,” Yahweh is the speaker and humankind is the object of the verb. The closing עֲשִׂיתִם, “I made them,” confirms the sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular, with the ending ־תִי.

analysis.evidence: In אֶמְחֶה … מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, עַל locates humankind on the surface of the ground. The prefix מֵ־ marks removal from that surface by the act of wiping out.
analysis.morphology: Preposition עַל with prefixed מֵ־ (from מִן).

analysis.evidence: פְּנֵי takes הָאֲדָמָה as its complement. The phrase מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה means “from the surface of the ground” and identifies where humanity will be wiped away.
analysis.morphology: Noun, common gender, plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “from the face of the ground,” הָאֲדָמָה completes the construct phrase פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה and identifies the surface from which living creatures will be wiped away.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth

analysis.evidence: In מֵאָדָם עַד בְּהֵמָה, “from humankind to livestock,” אָדָם designates humans collectively as the first group in a list that continues with creeping things and birds.
analysis.morphology: Preposition מִן in the form מֵ־ before א, followed by a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In מֵאָדָם עַד בְּהֵמָה, “from humans to livestock,” מִן marks the start of the range and the marked עַד includes livestock among those to be wiped out. The repeated עַד then extends the list to creeping things and birds.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: even to, extending the range to include a named category

analysis.evidence: In מֵאָדָם עַד בְּהֵמָה עַד רֶמֶשׂ וְעַד עוֹף הַשָּׁמָיִם, בְּהֵמָה names land beasts collectively alongside humans, creeping things, and birds. The list gives no indication that the beasts are specifically livestock.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The list begins with מֵאָדָם, “from humankind.” After בְּהֵמָה, “livestock,” the marked עַד introduces רֶמֶשׂ, “creeping things,” extending the scope of אֶמְחֶה, “I will wipe out,” to include them.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: even to, as many as, to the point of

analysis.evidence: The repeated עַד places רֶמֶשׂ between בְּהֵמָה (livestock) and עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם (birds of the sky). The singular noun names a class of creatures in the list.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The range begins with מֵאָדָם, “from humankind.” After livestock and creeping things, וְעַד introduces עוֹף הַשָּׁמָיִם, “the birds of the heavens,” as the final group included.
analysis.morphology: Preposition with prefixed conjunction וְ.
analysis.sense: even to, as many as, to the point of

analysis.evidence: עוֹף governs הַשָּׁמַיִם in the phrase עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, “birds of the sky.” It follows livestock and creeping things in the list of creatures to be wiped out.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In עוֹף הַשָּׁמָיִם, “birds of the sky,” the sky identifies where the birds fly. The phrase completes the verse’s list of creatures.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural noun in the absolute state with the prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: The marked כִּי introduces the reason for אֶמְחֶה (“I will wipe out”): “for I regret that I made them.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: YHWH gives the reason for his decision to wipe them out. The following כִּי עֲשִׂיתִם, “that I made them,” identifies the past action he regrets.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, first person common singular, with the subject ending ־תִּי

analysis.evidence: In נִחַמְתִּי כִּי עֲשִׂיתִם, “I regret that I made them,” the marked כִּי introduces עֲשִׂיתִם, the clause specifying what the speaker regrets.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected subordinating conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: עֲשִׂיתִם echoes בָּרָאתִי (“I created”) earlier in the verse. The plural object suffix refers to the humans and animals just listed, whom the speaker regrets having made.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular, with a third person masculine plural object suffix
